## Kyoto Family Trip at a Glance
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg

A 5-day Kyoto plan for 2 adults + 2 children, built for **slow pacing**, **few hotel changes**, and **kid-friendly variety**.
Budget target of **USD 3,500 excluding international flights** is very workable if you choose a mid-range family room/apartment and mix casual meals with a few nicer lunches.

## 5-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget Fit
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

| Day | Focus | Planned Highlights | Est. Steps | Local Transport | Meal Style | Est. Daily Cost |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | Higashiyama arrival day | Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, Yasaka area, early dinner | 7,000–9,000 | USD 10–18 | Casual lunch + family dinner | USD 220–320 |
| 2 | Arashiyama nature day | Bamboo Grove, Tenryu-ji garden, monkey park optional, river walk | 8,000–10,000 | USD 14–24 | Bento/cafe lunch | USD 230–340 |
| 3 | Hands-on culture day | Nishiki Market, tea ceremony or pottery class, Gion evening stroll | 6,000–8,500 | USD 10–18 | Market snacks + set meal | USD 260–380 |
| 4 | Temples + castle day | Nijo Castle, Kyoto Imperial Palace area, Kyoto Station/rail district | 6,000–9,000 | USD 12–20 | Easy lunch + noodle dinner | USD 210–310 |
| 5 | Fushimi / flexible final day | Fushimi Inari partial climb, sake district walk for adults, souvenir time | 7,000–9,500 | USD 12–22 | Early lunch + relaxed dinner | USD 220–330 |

### Day 1: Higashiyama Arrival and Easy Temple Start
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, store luggage, settle into one base hotel in central Kyoto.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** and keep it short; focus on the main temple grounds and nearby viewpoints.
- **Evening:** Walk Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka, then an early dinner in the Gion/Higashiyama area.
- **Kid-friendly meal:** Udon, tempura set, or a teishoku diner with rice, fish, and fried chicken.
- **Local transport estimate:** USD 10–18 for buses/taxis combined.

### Day 2: Arashiyama Nature and Easy Adventure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Bamboo Grove early, then **Tenryu-ji** gardens before crowds build.
- **Afternoon:** Choose one: **Iwatayama Monkey Park** for active kids, or a slower river walk and boat watching.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/A_Japanese_Macaque_at_Arashiyama_Monkey_Park_Iwatayama%2C_Japan.jpg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original Alt=Afternoon:** Choose one: **Iwatayama Monkey Park** for active kids, or a slower river walk and boat watching, Kyoto, Japan
- **Evening:** Return early for a relaxed dinner near your hotel.
- **Kid-friendly meal:** Bento lunch, curry rice, or a cafe with pancakes/omurice.
- **Local transport estimate:** USD 14–24, depending on train vs taxi segments.

### Day 3: Hands-On Kyoto Culture Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Morning:** Browse **Nishiki Market** for snacks, sweets, and light breakfast items.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original Alt=Morning:** Browse **Nishiki Market** for snacks, sweets, and light breakfast items, Kyoto, Japan
- **Afternoon:** Book **one hands-on activity** such as a family tea ceremony, pottery painting, or simple wagashi-making class.
- **Evening:** Short, calm walk through **Gion**; keep it low-step and photo-light.
- **Kid-friendly meal:** Market snacks plus a set meal with grilled chicken, rice, and miso soup.
- **Local transport estimate:** USD 10–18.

### Day 4: Temples, Castle, and a Low-Pressure City Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Nijo Castle** for history without too much walking.
- **Afternoon:** Relax around the Kyoto Imperial Palace area or return to the hotel for a rest break.
- **Evening:** Dinner near Kyoto Station, which gives many easy food choices for children.
- **Kid-friendly meal:** Ramen, donburi, or a family-friendly izakaya with non-spicy options.
- **Local transport estimate:** USD 12–20.

### Day 5: Fushimi Inari and Souvenir Finish
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- **Morning:** Do a **partial Fushimi Inari** visit; stop after the lower torii sections to stay within the step limit.
- **Afternoon:** Optional short walk in the Fushimi area or souvenir shopping near Kyoto Station.
- **Evening:** Final dinner close to your hotel and pack for departure.
- **Kid-friendly meal:** Sushi train, udon, or a casual Japanese grill.
- **Local transport estimate:** USD 12–22.

## Best Kyoto Neighborhoods for One Base Stay
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

| Neighborhood | Why It Works | Pros | Cons | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kyoto Station area | Best transport hub and easiest with kids | Fast train access; many restaurants; simple arrivals/departures | Less atmospheric than temple districts | Families prioritizing convenience |
| Gion / Higashiyama | Closest to temples and classic Kyoto scenery | Walkable to major sights; beautiful evenings; easy early starts | Hotels can cost more; busier streets | First-time visitors wanting charm |
| Kawaramachi / Shijo | Central, lively, and good for food | Great dining; easy access to transit; shopping nearby | Can feel busier and less quiet at night | Families who want food and flexibility |

### Recommended Base
- **Best overall:** **Kyoto Station area** for minimal stress, easiest transfers, and the simplest route management with children.
- **Best atmosphere:** **Gion/Higashiyama** if you want the most scenic stay and don’t mind a slightly higher nightly rate.
- **Best balance of food + transit:** **Kawaramachi/Shijo** if you want central access with lots of dining options.

## Budget Reality Check

- **Hotel/apartment:** USD 1,200–1,900 for 4 nights in a family room or 2-bedroom apartment
- **Local transport:** USD 60–100 total for the trip
- **Food:** USD 700–1,000 depending on how often you do sit-down dinners
- **Activities/entry fees:** USD 200–450
- **Buffer/souvenirs:** USD 200–400

A well-chosen family base should keep the total around **USD 2,400–3,850**, so your **USD 3,500** target is realistic with moderate dining and a mid-range stay.

## Output contract
- Return ONLY one JSON object. No prose, no markdown, no comments.
- Top-level shape:
  `{"root":"<id>","state":{...},"elements":{...}}`
- `root` must reference an existing key in `elements`.
- Every element object must contain:
  - `type` (component name from CATALOG)
  - `props` (object, can be empty)
  - `children` (array of element ids, can be empty)
- Every id in `children` must exist in `elements`.
- Use only component types listed in CATALOG.
- Supported actions: `openUrl`, `setState`, `pushState`, `removeState`, `validateForm`.
- Interaction bindings must use element-level `on` objects.
- Do NOT use legacy `props.action` or `functionCall`.
- Do NOT emit or use `className`.

## Hard rule: no legacy message array
- Correct output is a single flat object with `root/state/elements`.

## Markdown-to-IR conversion rule (strict)
- Do not emit literal markdown control tokens in `Text.props.text`:
  - no leading `#`, `##`, `###`
  - no literal table pipes (`|`) for table rows
  - no fenced code markers (``` or ''') inside `Text.props.text`; preserve the code body in `CodeBlock`/`ConsoleLog` props instead
  - avoid leaving raw `**bold**` markers in final text
- Convert markdown intent into UI structure:
  - headings -> `Text` with `variant` (`h1|h2|h3`)
  - table-like markdown -> compact `Table`
  - source code examples -> `CodeBlock` with `props.code` and `props.language`
  - terminal commands, console logs, and expected output -> `ConsoleLog` with `props.code` and `props.language: "console"`
  - emphasis -> plain text wording (or split into separate labeled/value text nodes)

## Positive format example

Valid (flat-spec):
```json
{
  "root": "main",
  "state": {},
  "elements": {
    "main": { "type": "Stack", "props": { "direction": "vertical", "gap": "md" }, "children": ["title"] },
    "title": { "type": "Text", "props": { "text": "Example", "variant": "h2" }, "children": [] }
  }
}
```

For explicit chart requests, use a compact `Chart` element backed by the same rows, not a placeholder chart image.

- For email/message-writing responses, use one compact `EmailPreview` element for the actual draft. Put `subject`, `to`, `from`, `date`, `role`, `company`, `body` paragraph array, and `signature` lines in props. Do not render email drafts as oversized generic Text paragraphs or detached Quick Actions cards.
- For product-description or marketing-copy responses, render a compact product landing screen: hero Card with inline Icon, 1-2 short body Text elements, feature/benefit cards, and only real URL-backed CTAs. Do not create standalone image galleries or use placeholder/random-host images.
- For programming/tutorial/debugging responses, separate source code from runtime output: use compact `CodeBlock` elements for functions/snippets and `ConsoleLog` elements for command lines, REPL transcripts, stack traces, and expected output. Do not render code or logs as oversized heading Text, and do not duplicate the same snippet as prose.
- Preserve all numbers, dates, times, units, and currency exactly.

## CATALOG

Layout:
- `Stack` props:
  - `direction`: `horizontal|vertical`
  - `gap`: `none|sm|md|lg|xl`
  - `align`: `start|center|end|stretch`
  - `justify`: `start|center|end|between|around`
  - `wrap` optional: `nowrap|wrap` (use with `direction: "horizontal"`)
  - `padding`, `paddingHorizontal`, `paddingVertical` optional numbers
  - `margin`, `marginHorizontal`, `marginVertical` optional numbers
  - `width`, `height`, `flex` optional numbers
- `List`
- `Card`

Content:
- `Text` props: `text` (required), `variant` optional (`h1|h2|h3|body|caption|chip|label`)
- `Formula` props: `latex` or `text` (required), optional `title`, `subtitle`, `result`, `display`. Use LaTeX-style notation for fractions, exponents, roots, and variables, for example `M = P \\frac{i(1+i)^n}{(1+i)^n - 1}`. Renderer formats fractions/exponents; do not use images for formulas.
- `CodeBlock` props: `code` (required), optional `language` (`python|javascript|kotlin|bash|text`) and `title`. Use for source code only; do not put expected output inside the same CodeBlock unless it is part of the source comment.
- `ConsoleLog` props: `code` (required), optional `language: "console"` and `title`. Use for terminal commands, REPL transcripts, stack traces, and expected output.
- `EmailPreview` props: `title`, `subtitle`, `subject`, `to`, `from`, `date`, `role`, `company`, `body` (string or paragraph array), `signature` (string or line array), optional `context`/`metadata`. Use for professional emails, drafts, messages, cover letters, and similar communication templates.
- `Table` props:
  - `columns` (required list of `{ "key": "...", "label": "..." }`)
  - `statePath` (preferred, pointer to row array in state) OR `rows` (inline row array)
  - `domain` optional (`weather|flight|booking|playlist|schedule|status|formula|comparison|generic`)
  - `preferredPresentation` optional (`cards|table`)
  - `primaryColumn` optional (key/label for portrait card title)
  - `highlightColumns` optional (list/string of 1-2 important key/label values)
  - `numericColumns` optional (list/string of numeric/currency/score/unit columns)
  - `entityMedia` optional for comparison/feature-matrix tables: map entity column key/label to `{ "image": "../assets/...", "alt": "..." }`; renderer shows these inside entity cards
  - `title`, `subtitle`, `mood`, `genre` optional for playlist/music table hero metadata
  - `sourceFormat` optional (`markdown|csv|tsv|html|plain`)
  - `sourceText` optional raw table text
- `Chart` props: `chartType` optional (`bar`), `columns`, `statePath` OR `rows`, `xKey`, `yKey`, optional `title`, `subtitle`, `yLabel`. Use this for generated charts instead of image placeholders.
- `Image` props: `url` (required), `fit` optional (`cover|contain`)
- `Icon` props: `name` (required, icon URL)
- `Video` props: `url` (required)
- `AudioPlayer` props: `url` (required), `description` optional
- `Divider`

Interactive:
- `Button` props: `label`, `variant` optional (`primary|borderless`)
- Use element-level `on.press` for button actions.
- `Tabs` props: `tabs` (required list of `{ "title": "...", "child": "<id>" }`)
- `Modal` props: `trigger` optional, `content` optional

Form:
- `TextField` props: `label` (required), `value` optional
- `CheckBox` props: `label` (required), `value` (required boolean)
- `ChoicePicker` props: `label` (required), `options` (required), `value` (required array)
- `Slider` props: `min`, `max`, `value` (required numbers), `label` optional
- `DateTimeInput` props: `value` (required), `label` optional, `enableDate` optional, `enableTime` optional
